done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

findings.body: Raise: Not done. Two worker rounds can leave the same review finding without triggering the required question. When a worker makes no code commit, close reuses the existing review, so `reviewed` stays the same; with no failing test, `tested_head` also stays the same. This equality check returns without counting the next round. The item can continue through repeated unchanged rounds indefinitely.
findings.title: Not done: repeated findings without code commits never stop the item

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The question derives “The worker tried” solely from commit subjects and prints “no new commits” when that list is empty. A worker can attempt a fix, leave the test failing, and finish without a commit. Forge then asks the owner without describing the attempt, which the Done-when line requires.
findings.title: Not done: the question omits what a worker without commits tried

findings.body: Raise: Functional. This stop check runs only after `worker.py:122` enters `machine.agent_slot`. As `machine.py:175-203` shows, another active worker and load of at least 1.5 per core can keep that call waiting. In that normal busy-machine case, Forge queues an item already due to stop and withholds its ready-to-ask question until a worker slot opens.
findings.title: Not done: a stuck item waits for a worker slot before asking the owner

stop.reason: Coordinator decision under the owner's bar: finding 1 (false re-count) is fixed at the current head; findings 2 (Jest tail key, Gain 2 Work 2 Harm 1) and 3 (refusal hint, Gain 2 Work 1 Harm 1) are recorded as lived-with

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
